blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.3
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.3

blocks.text: योनिवर्गः कलाशरीरम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] योनिवर्गः कलाशरीरम्

blocks.text: Yonivargaḥ kalāśarīram.
blocks.directed: Yonivargaḥ kalāśarīram.

blocks.text: The source and its multiplicity; that whose nature is limited activity.
blocks.directed: The source and its multiplicity; that whose nature is limited activity.

blocks.text: The Universe Has Three Different Ways to Ruin Your Day.
blocks.directed: The Universe Has Three Different Ways to Ruin Your Day.

blocks.text: Vasugupta now expands the explanation of bondage.
blocks.directed: Vasugupta now expands the explanation of bondage.

blocks.text: The sūtra is extremely compact. Kṣemarāja reads it in connection with the previous statement, “Knowledge is bondage,” and elaborates the remaining forms of impurity.
blocks.directed: The sūtra is extremely compact. Kṣemarāja reads it in connection with the previous statement, “Knowledge is bondage,” and elaborates the remaining forms of impurity.

blocks.text: Welcome to the three malas.
blocks.directed: Welcome to the three malas.

blocks.text: Āṇavamala — The impurity of smallness.
blocks.directed: Āṇavamala — The impurity of smallness.

blocks.text: The fundamental feeling of incompleteness.
blocks.directed: The fundamental feeling of incompleteness.

blocks.text: “I am only this.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am only this.”

blocks.text: “I am not enough.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am not enough.”

blocks.text: “I am this little subject rather than the limitless whole.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am this little subject rather than the limitless whole.”

blocks.text: The infinite has apparently decided to identify as a fraction of itself.
blocks.directed: The infinite has apparently decided to identify as a fraction of itself.

blocks.text: Māyīyamala — The impurity of differentiation.
blocks.directed: Māyīyamala — The impurity of differentiation.

blocks.text: Now consciousness doesn’t merely experience itself as limited.
blocks.directed: Now consciousness doesn’t merely experience itself as limited.

blocks.text: It experiences reality as divided into separate objects.
blocks.directed: It experiences reality as divided into separate objects.

blocks.text: This is mine.
blocks.directed: This is mine.

blocks.text: That’s yours.
blocks.directed: That’s yours.

blocks.text: That’s pleasant.
blocks.directed: That’s pleasant.

blocks.text: That’s disgusting.
blocks.directed: That’s disgusting.

blocks.text: That person disagrees with me and must therefore be metaphysically defective.
blocks.directed: That person disagrees with me and must therefore be metaphysically defective.

blocks.text: The world appears as a multiplicity of independently existing things.
blocks.directed: The world appears as a multiplicity of independently existing things.

blocks.text: Kārmamala — The impurity of limited agency and action.
blocks.directed: Kārmamala — The impurity of limited agency and action.

blocks.text: Now the individual acts within the limitations it experiences, generating further karmic involvement.
blocks.directed: Now the individual acts within the limitations it experiences, generating further karmic involvement.

blocks.text: “I did this.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I did this.”

blocks.text: “I must obtain that.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I must obtain that.”

blocks.text: “I have to correct what happened yesterday.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I have to correct what happened yesterday.”

blocks.text: And the entire machinery of conditioned experience keeps operating.
blocks.directed: And the entire machinery of conditioned experience keeps operating.

blocks.text: Notice the elegance.
blocks.directed: Notice the elegance.

blocks.text: First, I am limited.
blocks.directed: First, I am limited.

blocks.text: Then, the world is separate from me.
blocks.directed: Then, the world is separate from me.

blocks.text: Then, I am a limited agent who must act within this separate world.
blocks.directed: Then, I am a limited agent who must act within this separate world.

blocks.text: And suddenly you’ve got the entire human predicament.
blocks.directed: And suddenly you’ve got the entire human predicament.

blocks.text: The technical details of yoni, varga, and kalāśarīra belong to Trika’s theory of manifestation and its limited powers of agency, not merely a psychological metaphor. Kṣemarāja explicitly connects the sūtra with māyīyamala and kārmamala. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
